modern: Say nothing more to yourself than what the first appearances report. Suppose that it has been reported to you that a certain person speaks ill of you. This has been reported; but that you have been harmed, that has not been reported. I see that my child is sick. I do see it; but that he is in danger, I do not see. So always keep to the first appearances, and add nothing yourself from within, and then nothing happens to you. Or rather, add something, like a man who knows everything that happens in the world.
original: Say nothing more to thyself than what the first appearances report. Suppose that it has been reported to thee that a certain person speaks ill of thee. This has been reported; but that thou hast been injured, that has not been reported. I see that my child is sick. I do see; but that he is in danger, I do not see. Thus then always abide by the first appearances, and add nothing thyself from within, and then nothing happens to thee. Or rather add something like a man who knows everything that happens in the world.

notification_original: Say nothing more to thyself than what the first appearances report. Suppose that it has been reported to thee that a certain person speaks ill of thee.

explained.summary:
Don’t tell yourself more than your first impressions actually report. You hear someone criticised you: that’s what was reported, not that you’ve been harmed. You see your child is sick, not that they’re in danger. Stick to the plain facts and add nothing of your own, and nothing bad has happened to you.

If you must add anything, add the perspective of someone who knows how the world goes.
explained.today: A colleague says the boss ’wants a word’. That’s all you know, not that you’re in trouble. The test result is delayed; it doesn’t mean bad news. The friend hasn’t replied; it doesn’t mean they’re angry.
